title: Two-Year Gap Between Acquisition and Compensation Notices on the Gujarat Highways

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-83130 for the Second Gujarat State Highway Project (P114827). US$175 million approved 13 December 2013, loan agreement dated 12 February 2014, and the full loan amount disbursed. Original closing 31 January 2019, extended by 23 months in the restructuring of 13 September 2018; the project closed 31 December 2020. The borrower's contribution was US$158.50 million and the private sector's US$37.40 million. Component A, Highway Improvement, financed the road works and, within both of its sub-components, support for land acquisition and resettlement, utility relocation, environmental management and supervision. The appraisal document states that all land acquisition and resettlement costs paid in cash were to be met from Government of Gujarat funds, with Bank money covering the consultancies, goods and works for carrying out the resettlement plans. Classified Category A and triggered the Bank's policies on involuntary resettlement, indigenous peoples, forests and physical cultural resources (IEG ICR Review ICRR0022895, 13 June 2022; World Bank Project Appraisal Document, 7 November 2013).

title: 714 households moved for Hanoi's Ring Road 2
place: Ring Road 2 between Nhat Tan and Cau Giay, through Tay Ho, Cau Giay and Dong Da districts, Hanoi, Vietnam

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Hanoi Urban Transport Development Project, P083581. Credit IDA-43470 of US$155.21 million approved 3 July 2007. The commitment was revised down to US$115,901,593.10 and US$107,388,341.49 was disbursed. A linked Global Environment Facility grant, TF-58293 (P085393), committed US$9.8 million of which US$6,422,455 was disbursed. Borrower funding rose from US$139.68 million to US$329.3 million, of which US$181,409,261 was provided; total project cost at completion was US$295,220,057 against US$304.69 million at appraisal. Original closing date 31 December 2013, actual closing 31 December 2016, after restructurings on 6 November 2013, 11 June 2015 and 29 December 2016. The credit triggered Involuntary Resettlement policy OP/BP 4.12 (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 18 January 2018; Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review, 29 April 2018).

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA), safeguards finding
lenders.role: Bank supervision missions rated social safeguard performance moderately satisfactory, and moderately unsatisfactory where non-compliance was found. The mid-term review found that the project management unit and mainly district authorities had followed Hanoi People's Committee regulations rather than the agreed Resettlement Policy Framework and Resettlement Action Plan: no assistance for households on land classed as illegal residential land, replacement cost that did not replace what affected households lost, a cut-off date set earlier under the Land Law, disputed eligibility for compensation where land occupation was classed as illegal, and no assistance for unregistered businesses (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 18 January 2018).
